title: Review of c40's wide local fuel cut: replicated on seed 10, the 0.75x-nearest-neighbour kF=0 disk kills 1 of 4 targets and starves 3 to remnants of 19-24% of fed size, with every body outside kept
summary: Fresh labkit seed 10 of the unchanged world (t=12000: 6 nucleations, 9 persistent splits, generation 2, 0 merges, s layer on 69/72 individuals). From its t=12000 frame I branched a fed twin and one arm per target for the 4 bodies with the farthest neighbours (cutmany.py: kF=0 in a disk of 0.75x the nearest-neighbour distance, 33-34 px, the finding's rule) for 1500 t. Target 0: 205 -> 52 px by t=12300 and 0 by t=13475 (dead); targets 1-3: 206-228 -> 42-50 px (19-24% of fed 210-234 px), alive at t=13475. The 15 bodies outside the disk stay in every arm; mean F inside the disk only falls 0.81 -> 0.64-0.68. This reproduces the finding's two outcomes (death on some targets, a starved remnant on others); my seed 9 run (20261026T1501-c44-review-cips-layered cut_s9) gave the same 1 of 4.

observations.E: cutw_s10.json: target 0 dead by t=13475 (205 -> 0 px), targets 1-3 at 42-50 px vs fed 210-234 px; 15 outside bodies kept in every arm; fed twin keeps all 16

seeds_run.result: pass: 1/4 targets dead, 3/4 starved remnants, neighbours kept (as in the finding: death on 1 of 2 seeds)

controls_run.E: cutw_s10 fed twin branched from the same t=12000 state

verdicts.limitation: Branch state rebuilt from labkit's float16 frame at t=12000; targets chosen by my rule (farthest neighbours), not the finding's single target. The finding is right that this disk is not a clean kill: fuel diffuses in across the edge (F in the disk stays at 0.64), so most targets survive shrunken; an absorbing moat makes it decisive (20261026T1525-c44-cips-moat-cut).
